text: Because gravity in general relativity is a genuine force, the geodesic equation of motion ẍ^μ + Γ^μ_νρ ẋ^ν ẋ^ρ = 0 must depend explicitly on the mass of the falling body, just as Newton's second law does.
explanation: This is false on both counts the book stresses. Gravity in GR is not a force but the curvature of spacetime, and free fall is force-free geodesic motion. The geodesic equation contains no reference to the particle's mass at all, which is precisely why every body falls identically in a given spacetime — the equivalence principle expressed geometrically.
